title: Help & Support
subtitle: Product help, usage guidance and support contact.

gettingStarted.title: Getting Started
gettingStarted.body: Sign in with the email and password your administrator set up for you. On the Dashboard, use Clock In to start your shift and Clock Out to end it - a live map above the button shows your current position and, when relevant, the site's own geofence circle. Your organization's site(s) and any camera/GPS requirements are configured by your administrator.

attendance.title: Clocking In & Out
attendance.body: Choose your site (and project, if applicable) before clocking in - or leave Site empty and describe where you actually are if you're not at a registered location. Some sites require a photo. Right before anything is submitted, a confirmation screen shows exactly what's about to be recorded - your photo (if one was taken), your detailed GPS location, the site/workplace, and the time - with two optional fields, a note and what you're working on (activity), that get saved with that clock-in or clock-out and are visible to your manager.

walkInGeofence.title: Working at a Site You're Not Assigned To
walkInGeofence.body: If you're physically standing inside a registered site's geofence today but aren't formally assigned there, it's suggested to you automatically in the Site list (marked as "you're here today") - useful if you genuinely work at a different site every day. Clocking in with no site at all still works too: your own clock-in point becomes the center of an organization-wide radius for the rest of that shift, giving you the same real-time protection a registered site's geofence already provides, even somewhere that was never set up as a site.

siteChange.title: Changing Sites Mid-Shift
siteChange.body: Moving to a different site without clocking out entirely: press Pause before you leave your current site. The button becomes Change Site - press it once you've arrived at the next one, and the move is recorded in your attendance history with the time it happened. The button then goes back to being Pause, ready for the next time you move.

sos.title: SOS / Emergency
sos.body: Available while presence monitoring is active for your shift. Pressing it immediately sends a high-priority alert to your managers with your last known location, and is logged as a real emergency record - reserved for genuine safety situations, not a general-purpose button.

notifications.title: How Notifications Reach the Right Person
notifications.body: If you clock in or out - or move around during your shift - outside your assigned work area, you're asked to explain why, and the right person is notified automatically: an ordinary employee's situation reaches that site's own manager (and the Owner); a manager's own situation escalates straight to the Owner instead of to fellow managers; the Owner, answering to no one, is never flagged at all. Tap a notification to jump straight to what it's about.

timesheets.title: Timesheets
timesheets.body: Once your manager generates a timesheet for a period, it appears under Timesheets for you to review and submit for approval. Worked time, breaks and overtime are shown as separate totals - break time is never subtracted from your worked hours, and overtime is based on the start time your site's own policy defines. Once approved, a timesheet is locked - if you believe it needs a correction, you can request one from the timesheet's own page, and an approved correction genuinely updates the recorded time it applies to.

exceptions.title: Exceptions & Corrections - What Approval Actually Means
exceptions.body: An out-of-zone exception or a correction request isn't just a paper decision anymore: if your manager approves it, you're treated as present the full time with no penalty. If it's rejected - whether before or after you've explained yourself - your effective worked time is capped at the moment the situation was first detected, which reduces the hours and overtime your timesheet ends up counting for that day.

allowances.title: Allowances
allowances.body: Open Allowances from the sidebar and pick a date to add an entry - the date, site and clock-in/out are filled in automatically. Fill in meal, transportation, housing and other amounts yourself, then Submit. A manager or the Owner approves or rejects it; while it's a draft you can still edit and re-save it. Overtime hours/days are computed automatically from your site's shift policy, if one is configured.

kiosk.title: Kiosk Mode
kiosk.body: Open Kiosk Mode from the sidebar and pick a site to launch its shared clock-in screen - meant for a tablet or computer at the entrance, not your own personal device. Select your name from the list, enter your personal kiosk PIN, then Clock In or Clock Out. Your kiosk PIN is separate from your login password - set or change it from the Dashboard, or an administrator/manager can set it for you from your profile page under People.

reportsCenter.title: Reports Center
reportsCenter.body: Reports gathers report generation in one place: pick a report type (Attendance Record or Allowances), a date range and, if relevant, an employee, then export it as a PDF - the same export already available on each of those pages, just with one dedicated place to reach for any of them. Timesheets are generated, submitted and exported from their own Timesheets page instead, since a timesheet belongs to one specific employee and period rather than a date range.

sites.title: Sites (Administrators)
sites.body: Sites (Owner/Manager only) is where worksites are set up and where employees/managers are assigned to one: name, address, GPS coordinates and radius, time zone, kiosk mode, and whether attendance/geofence/camera are required there. A site's actual behavior - GPS accuracy tolerance, grace period, shift hours, overtime/late-deduction timing, break rounding, both self-service block toggles, and exempt employees - is configured from Settings instead, not from this form.

settingsCenter.title: Settings (Owner)
settingsCenter.body: A real home for organization-wide configuration: the no-site geofence radius; the site policy defaults (GPS accuracy tolerance, break rounding, grace period) a brand-new site starts from, since these are almost always the same across an organization rather than something that genuinely differs site to site; Site Policy itself - pick any site from a dropdown to review or change its own GPS tolerance, grace period, shift hours, overtime/late-deduction timing, break rounding, both self-service block toggles, and exempt employees, all in one place instead of hunting through that site's own page; and Payroll Integration (QuickBooks Online). API keys for connecting other PROSM products now have their own dedicated page in the sidebar instead of living here.

leave.title: Leave (PTO)
leave.body: Request time off from the Leave page - pick a type (Annual, Sick, Unpaid, Emergency, Other), a date range and an optional reason. Only Annual leave tracks a real entitled/used/remaining balance (21 days a year by default - an Owner can raise or lower a specific employee's own entitlement from their profile page under People, e.g. for legally-required increases tied to long tenure); every other type just shows how many days you've taken this year, with no fixed cap. Your manager or the Owner reviews pending requests from the Manager Console, and can also revoke an already-approved request from there if plans change - you'll be notified either way. Approved leave counts toward your generated timesheet for that period.

schedule.title: Shift Roster
schedule.body: See your own upcoming shifts from the sidebar's Shift Roster page - everyone can see their own. Managers with scheduling authority can additionally set up reusable shift templates per site (e.g. "Morning", "Night") and assign specific employees to specific shifts, including real overnight shifts that cross midnight (shown with a "(+1)" marker) - the system checks for overlapping shifts automatically, even across a midnight boundary.

calendar.title: Hijri or Gregorian Calendar
calendar.body: Every date shown in the app can display as Gregorian or Hijri - pick your preference from the user menu at the bottom of the sidebar, next to Language and Appearance. This is a per-device preference, not an organization-wide setting - each person can choose their own.

payrollIntegration.title: Payroll Integration (Owner)
payrollIntegration.body: From Settings > Payroll Integration, connect your organization's own QuickBooks Online company to automatically send verified worked hours across, matched to QuickBooks employees by email. This is a one-time connection each organization sets up for itself - here's exactly what happens: (1) you press Connect QuickBooks; (2) a new tab opens showing QuickBooks' own real sign-in screen; (3) you sign in with your own QuickBooks account (not PROSM's) and approve the connection on QuickBooks' own consent screen; (4) QuickBooks sends you back to PROSM Time's server, which exchanges that approval for a secure connection - no one, not even you, can view the underlying keys afterward, only PROSM Time's own server ever uses them; (5) back in PROSM Time, the card now shows your company's real name, confirming the connection is live. From then on, "Sync now" pushes newly completed, verified shifts across - hours already sent are never duplicated on a later sync. No one else can complete this connection on your behalf, since it's your own company's payroll data.

permissions.title: Permissions (Administrators)
permissions.body: Each person's page under People shows their real granted permissions and lets an authorized administrator grant, revoke, or reset an individual permission with a reason - visible only to those who already hold that authority. The Owner always has every permission; other roles start from a default bundle that can be adjusted per person.

desktopApp.title: Windows Desktop App
desktopApp.body: The same PROSM Time you already know, installed as a real Windows program. It opens filling your screen; F11 switches to true fullscreen and Escape always brings back the normal window with its close button. Your sign-in stays remembered between launches, exactly like on your phone or in a browser.

liveMap.title: Live Map
liveMap.body: The Dashboard shows a real, theme-aware map with your current position - and, once you're clocked in or have a site selected, a translucent circle marking that site's real geofence, so you can see at a glance where you stand relative to it before you even try to clock in or out.

radio.title: Why There's a Radio in PROSM Time
radio.body: The Radio isn't a distraction from attendance - it's built around it. Play a station during your commute, and PROSM Time is already open and on your mind the moment you arrive: instead of the app being something you have to remember to open once you're at your desk, it's already there in your hand, and Clock In is right where you left it. It's a small, deliberate nudge against the single most common attendance mistake - simply forgetting to clock in on time.

q1.question: I forgot to clock out - what do I do?
q1.answer: Contact an administrator or manager - they can record the correct Clock Out on your behalf, and the action is recorded as theirs, not yours. A manager can also submit a correction request on an already-recorded time, which - once approved - genuinely updates it.

q2.question: Why was my Clock In flagged as outside my work area?
q2.answer: Your site has a configured geofence and GPS accuracy tolerance (or, with no site selected, your organization's own no-site radius around where you clocked in). If your reported location fell outside that area, you're asked to explain why so the right manager can review it - approving it clears the flag entirely; rejecting it caps your worked time at that moment.

q3.question: Can I use the app while offline?
q3.answer: Clock In and Clock Out are queued locally if you lose connectivity and sync automatically once you're back online - you'll see a pending-sync notice until it's confirmed.

q4.question: How do I change the language or theme?
q4.answer: Open the user menu (bottom of the sidebar) - Language and Appearance (Dark/Light/System) can be changed there at any time, and you can also set your profile picture from the same menu.

q5.question: I clocked in without choosing a site - why did it ask for a "workplace"?
q5.answer: Site is optional so you can register attendance from your real current location even when it isn't a registered site - but a short description of where you actually are is required in that case, so reports never show a blank site. Your organization's own no-site radius still protects that session the same way a real site's geofence would.

q6.question: What's the difference between Attendance Record and Timesheets?
q6.answer: Attendance Record is a live, date-ranged log of clock-in/out events - nothing to approve. Timesheets are a generated, period-based object (worked/break/overtime totals) that goes through a real submit -> approve workflow and gets locked once approved.

q7.question: Can I export my attendance or timesheet as a PDF?
q7.answer: Yes - Attendance Record, Timesheets and Allowances each have their own Export PDF action, scoped to whatever you're currently viewing, and Reports gathers the Attendance Record and Allowances exports in one dedicated place too.

q8.question: Why can't I see some employees in People or Attendance Record?
q8.answer: You only ever see yourself, plus - if you manage a site - the people assigned to that site. The Owner sees everyone. This is enforced by the server, not just hidden in the interface.

q9.question: Does the desktop app sign me out every time I close it?
q9.answer: No - your session is remembered between launches, the same way it is on your phone or in a browser.

q10.question: Can I still play the radio while I'm clocked in?
q10.answer: Yes - it keeps playing in the background regardless of your attendance status. It lives in the sidebar's Media row (tap it to expand the station list and search) rather than the header, and takes up very little space when collapsed.
